b.answer:
Worked example: Harvest Lane needs Paystack's list of Nigerian banks so riders' and suppliers' bank names are picked from a list, not typed.

The cURL from the docs (check the current page; examples change):

curl https://api.paystack.co/bank?currency=NGN \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_SECRET_KEY" \
  -X GET
  • curl: the tool that sends the request
  • https://api.paystack.co/bank: the endpoint
  • ?currency=NGN: a query parameter
  • -H "Authorization: Bearer …": a header carrying the secret key
  • -X GET: the method

In n8n: Manual Trigger → Edit Fields (currency = NGN) → HTTP Request → Import cURL. Then:

  1. Delete the imported Authorization header.
  2. Authentication: Generic credential type → Header Auth → new credential "Paystack test": Name Authorization, Value Bearer sk_test_… (your test key, typed only into the credential).
  3. Change the currency query value from NGN to {{ $json.currency }}. Set it to GHS in Edit Fields and the same node lists Ghanaian banks.

Result: one item with status: true and a data list of banks. Screenshot the node: the headers list is empty and the key appears nowhere.
mistakes: Leaving the imported Authorization header in place, so it overrides the credential (or exposes the key).
Using a live secret key instead of a test key while practising.
Replacing nothing with an expression, or replacing a value that isn't meant to change (the endpoint path).
Not being able to say what -H and -X do in the original command.
b.pass: The request returns data, the node's headers and URL contain no secret (only a credential is selected), one value is an expression with a working preview, and every part of the cURL is named in the log.
b.redo: Send it back if a key is visible anywhere in the node or screenshots, or the request only works with the pasted header.

s.answer:
Worked example: Harvest Lane practises both pagination styles before the real supplier API arrives.

1. DummyJSON (offset). The solved workflow: skip = {{ $pageCount * 50 }}, complete when {{ $response.body.products.length < 50 }}, max 20 pages, 500 ms interval. Split Out on products.

2. Rick and Morty (next URL). HTTP Request, GET https://rickandmortyapi.com/api/character. Options → Pagination:

SettingValue
ModeResponse Contains Next URL
Next URL{{ $response.body.info.next }}
Pagination Complete WhenOther: {{ !$response.body.info.next }} (next is null on the last page, so the response is not empty)
Limit Pages FetchedOn, max 60
Interval Between Requests500 ms

Then Split Out on results, then Remove Duplicates comparing the field id.

Counts for the log (your numbers may differ if the APIs have changed; compare with what the API itself reports):

APIAPI's own totalPages fetchedItems after Split OutAfter Remove Duplicates
DummyJSONtotal on page 1, e.g. 1944194194
Rick and Mortyinfo.count, e.g. 826info.pages, e.g. 42826826

If Remove Duplicates drops anything, your first page was fetched twice. If the count is short, your stop rule fired early or the page limit is too low.
mistakes: Using "Response is empty" as the stop rule for the next-URL API, which never returns an empty response, so it runs to the page limit.
Starting the DummyJSON offset at $pageCount + 1, skipping the first product.
Counting pages instead of items after Split Out.
Skipping the duplicate check and claiming the count matches.
s.pass: Both workflows' item counts after Split Out equal the API's own total (DummyJSON total, Rick and Morty info.count), a Remove Duplicates node or sheet formula shows no duplicates, and both use a page limit and an interval.
s.redo: Send it back if either count is off, duplicates exist, or a page count is hard-coded.

g.answer:
Worked example: Harvest Lane reads invoices from Zoho Books, which (at the time of writing) has no dedicated n8n node. Check the provider's docs for current URLs, scopes and your account's data-centre domain.

Credential: Generic OAuth2 API "Zoho Books (HL)"

  • Grant type: Authorization Code
  • Authorization URL: https://accounts.zoho.com/oauth/v2/auth
  • Access Token URL: https://accounts.zoho.com/oauth/v2/token
  • Client ID and Client Secret: from the app registered in Zoho's API console, where n8n's OAuth Redirect URL was pasted exactly
  • Scope: ZohoBooks.invoices.READ (read-only: the least access that does the job)
  • Auth URI query parameters: access_type=offline, so Zoho issues a refresh token

Workflow: Schedule (daily 08:00) → Edit Fields "Settings" (org_id) → HTTP Request GET https://www.zohoapis.com/books/v3/invoices?organization_id={{ $json.org_id }}, Authentication: Generic → OAuth2 → that credential. Options → Response: Include Response Headers and Status on, Never Error on. Then IF {{ $json.statusCode }} equals 429: true → Wait 60 s → a second HTTP Request (one retry) → if still not 200, email Tolu. False → Split Out body.invoices → sheet.

Evidence table:

CheckResult
Day 1 run200, 37 invoices
Day 2 run, no reconnect200, 41 invoices (token refreshed itself)
Forced 429 (pinned response edited to statusCode 429)Took the wait branch, retry succeeded

Submit: both Executions screenshots with dates, the IF branch screenshot, and the half-page guide: register the app, copy the redirect URL, fill the six credential fields, connect, test one call, what 401 and 429 mean.
mistakes: Missing the offline or refresh setting the provider requires, so the connection dies when the first access token expires.
Requesting broad write scopes when read-only would do.
Treating every non-200 as a 429 and retrying 401s forever.
Writing the guide from memory without testing it, so a step (like the exact redirect URL) is wrong.
g.pass: Two successful executions at least a day apart with no reconnect, a working 429 branch (shown with a real or simulated 429), and a half-page guide another learner could follow step by step.
g.redo: Send it back if the token needed reconnecting, the 429 path was never exercised, or the guide is missing the app registration or redirect steps.
